newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Dec 16.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Dec 16.

text.p: Three of Mexico's major ports were shut on Monday as of 1000 local/1600 GMT, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in a daily update.
In Tamaulipas state, winds with speeds of 55 to 65 km per hour closed the ports of Altamira and Tampico, and wind speeds of 65 to 75 km per hour shut down the port of Tuxpan.

Smaller ships were prohibited from sailing at La Pesca and Matamoros in Tamaulipas state and Salina Cruz in Oaxaca state. Port captains warned against smaller boats sailing from the coast of Tamaulipas, northern Veracruz and Tabasco because of high waves and winds.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.

Light rains and disperse wind gusts along the southern Baja California peninsula, the states of Sonora, Sinaloa, Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima and Michoacan. Winds from the north and northeast at 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 kms/11 to 17 miles per hour) with waves reaching three to five feet high.
In the Gulf of Tehuantepec northeast winds were clocked at 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 kms/17 to 22 miles per hour) with wave heights at five to nine feet.

Light cold front heading south-southwest to the northeastern Gulf of Mexico at a speed of 28 kms/17 miles per hour. Northern winds are between 20 and 25 knots (38 to 47 kms/22 to 38 miles per hour) with waves of four to nine feet high.
Isolated showers along the coast of Quintana Roo and winds from the east and southeast of 10 to 15 knots with waves three to five feet high.
